title: Towards Scalable High-Voltage Battery Packs: A Modular Architecture Enabled by Dual Active Bridge Converters
abstract: The growing adoption of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) has increased the demand for scalable architectures that convert low-voltage (LV) battery packs into high-voltage (HV) configurations. However, series connection of LV packs is limited by the voltage ratings of their embedded Battery Management System (BMS) and protection circuitry. This paper proposes a modular Smart Battery architecture based on isolated Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC–DC converters, which provide galvanic isolation, bidirectional power flow and independent voltage regulation for each LV battery module, allowing commercial LV packs to be integrated into an HV DC-link without hardware modifications. A master BMS controller performs State of Charge (SoC) balancing by adjusting the individual DAB output-voltage references through a proportional balancing law, while local proportional–integral (PI) controllers regulate the module output voltages. Functional performance was evaluated through PLECS simulations and controller hardware-in-the-loop (C-HIL) tests with four modules forming a 192-V dc link. The results demonstrate dc-link regulation under load transients and SoC equalization under the evaluated initial imbalances and capacity mismatches, supporting the coordinated-control implementation on the physical DSP against the real-time power-stage model.
title_zh: Towards Scalable High-Voltage Battery Packs: A Modular Architecture Enabled by Dual Active Bridge Converters

title: Development of a Data-Driven Model or Predicting the State of Health of the Li-ion Battery in an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are a key enabler of sustainable aviation, yet their gradual degradation poses a critical safety and reliability challenge, particularly for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating in high-temperature environments. This study develops a data-driven model for predicting the State of Health (SOH) of Li-ion batteries using machine learning (ML). The NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE) Li-ion Battery Aging Dataset (Battery #5) was used to train and test a Random Forest (RF) regression model, with features selected to capture the effects of high-temperature operation and voltage behavior. The proposed RF model was benchmarked against a Linear Regression (LR) baseline and achieved highly accurate SOH estimation, with a coefficient of determination (R^2 score) of 0.9077 and low error values, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.2578 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.2185. These results also provide a reliable foundation for estimating the battery's Remaining Useful Life (RUL). The proposed approach supports UAV reliability and safer flight operations in high-temperature environments.
title_zh: Development of a Data-Driven Model or Predicting the State of Health of the Li-ion Battery in an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle

title: Adaptive Fuzzy Balancing Control for Vehicle-Mounted Battery Strings Based on a Hierarchical Buck–Boost Topology
abstract: Cell-to-cell inconsistency remains a critical engineering bottleneck for lithium-ion battery strings in vehicle-mounted energy storage systems and is especially acute in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) auxiliary storage packs, where gravimetric energy density, charging turnaround, and balancing precision directly govern mission endurance and payload capacity. Conventional single-layer adjacent Buck–Boost topologies suffer from long energy transfer paths, high cumulative losses, and slow convergence under severe mismatch. This work pairs an improved hierarchical bidirectional Buck–Boost topology with a multi-constraint adaptive fuzzy controller. The two-layer shared-bus topology enables direct inter-module energy transfer with minimal additional components, while the controller takes SOC deviation as its primary input, embeds terminal voltage as a safety boundary in the fuzzy rule base, and tunes equalization intensity via a standard-deviation adaptive gain. Simulations on an 8-cell, 2-module system show that intra-module convergence time (max cell-to-cell SOC deviation ≤3%) falls by an average of 47% versus the conventional baseline. The fuzzy controller further reduces convergence time by 32.7% (35.0% for Module 1, 30.4% for Module 2) and shortens full-charging time by 15.4% (from ~1300 s to 1100 s) relative to the topology-only scheme, supporting its potential for vehicle-mounted battery management applications.
title_zh: Adaptive Fuzzy Balancing Control for Vehicle-Mounted Battery Strings Based on a Hierarchical Buck–Boost Topology

title: Explainable Machine Learning Algorithms for State-of-Health Estimation and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction address related but distinct aspects of lithium-ion battery degradation. This study evaluates separate XGBoost regressors for SOH estimation and RUL prediction using four NASA Ames lithium-ion cells with complete capacity-fade trajectories. The reference capacity is defined as the median capacity of the first five discharges, while end of life (EOL) is defined as the first subsequent cycle at which capacity falls to or below 80% of this reference. At a fixed observation point of 600~s, the prediction features comprise electrical, thermal, cycle-related, initial-reference, and preceding electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements. Full-discharge capacity and future EOL information are used only to construct retrospective target labels and are excluded from the corresponding predictors. A leave-one-cell-out evaluation yields 351 evaluated cycles. XGBoost achieves pooled SOH and RUL mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 1.157 percentage points and 17.948 cycles, respectively, while ridge regression achieves 1.195 percentage points and 17.611 cycles. The held-out B0006 cell exhibits a substantially higher XGBoost RUL MAE of 34.886 cycles, highlighting the limitations of cross-cell prognostic transfer despite low pooled SOH error. TreeSHAP analysis identifies the change in 600-s voltage relative to the cell's initial reference as the largest average contribution to SOH predictions. Removing this feature increases SOH root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 1.473 to 2.929 percentage points, while reducing RUL RMSE from 22.731 to 20.836 cycles. These findings demonstrate that feature importance and predictive utility differ between SOH estimation and RUL prediction.
title_zh: Explainable Machine Learning Algorithms for State-of-Health Estimation and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries

title: Unveiling Ghost Features in Battery Safety AI: Generalization Auditing for Sim-to-Real Thermal Runaway Prediction
abstract: Abstract Reliable early warning of lithium-ion battery thermal runaway (TR) requires predictive models that remain robust under abuse-condition variations and simulation-to-reality (Sim-to-Real) domain shifts. This study proposes a Generalization Audit Framework (GAF) that converts cross-domain disparities into feature-resolved diagnostics. GAF integrates Feature Fingerprint Distance (FFD) to quantify shifts in model attribution topology and a Ghost Feature Vulnerability Index (GFVI) to rank feature-level coupling distortions between synthetic and real-world domains. Validation using Doyle-Fuller-Newman (DFN)-based synthetic scenarios and experimental overcharge data from NCM622 18650 cells shows that thermal-domain features dominate model attribution (55.3%–76.3%), while voltage- and current-dependent descriptors exhibit concentrated cross-domain instability. A Type-I/Type-II taxonomy further distinguishes refinable kinetic mismatches from structural discrepancies associated with unmodeled discrete device states. Guided by these diagnostics, pruning the four highest-GFVI features together with binary risk reformulation improves Patch-Transformer zero-shot cross-abuse Macro-F1 from 0.821 ± 0.012 to 0.888 ± 0.009. With 10% target-domain data for adaptation, the lightweight model (110,820 parameters) achieves F1 = 0.951. GAF therefore provides a diagnosis-to-mitigation workflow for identifying and reducing cross-domain vulnerabilities in battery safety prediction.
title_zh: Unveiling Ghost Features in Battery Safety AI: Generalization Auditing for Sim-to-Real Thermal Runaway Prediction
